content: Ceftriaxone is a medication used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as cephalosporin antibiotics. This drug is not recommended for use in newborns with high blood bilirubin levels or in premature infants due to an increased risk of side effects. This medication is administered via injection into a muscle or vein, as directed by your doctor, typically once or twice daily. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you have been properly instructed by your healthcare professional on its preparation and administration. Before using ceftriaxone, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. If either is present, do not use the liquid. If you are using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the bag at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow it to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw the solution using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the bag well and check for leaks by squeezing it. Discard the solution if the bag leaks. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue using the medication for the full duration prescribed, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may allow bacteria to continue growing, potentially leading to a relapse of the infection. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, or pain at the injection site. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, ceftriaxone may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. If ceftriaxone is mixed with a numbing medication (such as lidocaine) before injection into a muscle, it may rarely cause a serious blood problem known as methemoglobinemia. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare but possible. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. Before using ceftriaxone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other antibiotics (such as penicillins or other cephalosporins), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Do not administer products containing calcium (including IV solutions such as Ringer's solution, Hartmann's solution, or parenteral nutrition like TPN/PPN) to a newborn less than one month old who is receiving this medication. Ceftriaxone may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). Inform your healthcare provider if you are scheduled to receive any vaccines. This medication passes into breast milk in small amounts and is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Ceftriaxone may interfere with certain lab tests (such as urine glucose tests), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using this medication, lab and/or medical tests (such as complete blood count and kidney function tests) should be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
